The patent described 'the method of, and apparatus for, transmitting vocal or other sounds telegraphically.' Several walls were built from as early as the 7th century BC, with selective stretches later joined together by Qin Shi Huang (220–206 BC), the first emperor of China. Little of the Qin wall remains. Later on, many successive dynasties built and maintained multiple stretches of border walls. The most well-known sections of the wall were built by the Ming dynasty (1368–1644). A 2012 survey found that the Ming walls measure 8,850 km (5,500 mi), while the total length of all walls across all dynasties measures 21,196 km (13,171 mi).
judgments.evidence: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications that were built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states and Imperial China as protection against various nomadic groups from the Eurasian Steppe.
judgments.reason: L'evidenza ripete esattamente la descrizione del claim, aggiungendo solo un dettaglio sulla finalità che non cambia il supporto logico.

judgments.passage_text: Qin Shi Huang (259–210 BC) was the founder of the Qin dynasty and the first emperor of a unified China. He is credited with ordering the construction of the first version of the Great Wall of China, connecting and extending existing walls built by the Warring States. The original Qin walls, built largely of tamped earth and wood, were intended to protect the northern borders from Xiongnu invasions. Very little of the original Qin wall remains today, as it was built from perishable materials.

per_claim.claim: Charles Darwin developed the theory of evolution.

judgments.passage_text: Charles Robert Darwin (12 February 1809 – 19 April 1882) was an English naturalist, geologist and biologist, best known for his contributions to the science of evolution. His proposition that all species of life have descended from common ancestors is now widely accepted and considered a fundamental concept in science. In a joint presentation with Alfred Russel Wallace, he introduced his scientific theory that this branching pattern of evolution resulted from a process that he called natural selection. His 1859 book On the Origin of Species established evolutionary theory.

The book was published on 24 November 1859, by John Murray. The first edition of 1,250 copies sold out the same day. per_claim.claim: The nuclear arms race at its peak involved approximately 70,000 global nuclear warheads.

judgments.passage_text: The nuclear arms race was a competition for supremacy in nuclear warfare between the United States, the Soviet Union, and their respective allies during the Cold War. The arms race led to the development of the intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM), nuclear submarines, and the concept of mutually assured destruction (MAD). At its peak in 1986, global nuclear warhead stockpiles numbered approximately 70,000.

per_claim.claim: The Cold War ended with the dissolution of the Soviet Union on December 26, 1991.

judgments.passage_text: The Cold War was a period of geopolitical tension between the United States and the Soviet Union and their respective allies, the Western Bloc and the Eastern Bloc. It began following the end of World War II in 1947 and lasted until the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991. The conflict was characterized by political and military rivalry, ideological opposition between capitalism and communism, proxy wars in Korea, Vietnam, and elsewhere, and a nuclear arms race. While the two superpowers never engaged in direct warfare, the Cold War shaped world politics for nearly five decades.
